evidence_quotes.two_concerns_question: since we talked to a lot of different customers everyday some of their concerns are movers not arriving on time or damages to their items. Are any of these or concerns as well?
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Customer deflected the concern question ('I assume it shouldn't be a concern of mine. It would be a concern of you all') and Joanna did not probe deeper or follow up with 'tell me more about that'—she moved directly to the promises instead.
evidence_quotes.value_days: if we're going to do it on Tuesday, it's actually our lowest hourly rate for the week which is $104 per hour, per mover. And we recommend two guys for your move. So that's $208 per hour. [Identifies lowest rate day, states saving relative to other days; no explicit dollar-amount savings offered or date flexibility asked because the customer is already on the best value day.]
evidence_quotes.rate_lock_then_ask: Never asked. Call ends with 'I'll still send you the quotation just in case if anything changes, just let us know, okay?' — no rate lock, no explicit ask for the business, no booking attempt.

top_strength: Joanna collected comprehensive logistics details (addresses, floor numbers, parking, item list, packing needs) in a systematic, conversational way that set up an accurate estimate.
coaching_note: Step 6 and 7 were skipped entirely—there was no final concerns check after pricing, no rate lock statement, and no explicit ask for the business. When a customer says they'll shop around, the next move is to reinforce the rate lock and close with a clear ask, not to end the call.
